properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 10 at 9:46PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Horse Creek near Arcadia at SR 72.

* WHEN...From Sunday morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The access road to Hidden Oak is
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Thursday the stage was 7.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Sunday
morning and continue rising to 12.2 feet Sunday evening.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.2
feet on 11/24/1997.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT FROM SUNDAY MORNING UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 11 at 12:32AM EDT until September 11 at 4:30AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
FFWRLX

The National Weather Service in Charleston has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Braxton County in north central West Virginia...
Central Gilmer County in north central West Virginia...
Northwestern Upshur County in northeastern West Virginia...
Lewis County in northern West Virginia...

* Until 430 AM EDT.

* At 1232 AM EDT, doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the
warned area. Between 0.75 and 1.25 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned
area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Buckhannon, Weston, Stonewall Jackson, Cedar Creek State Park,
Burnsville, Sand Fork, Sand Run, Camden, Walkersville, Alum Bridge,
Horner, Linn, Stouts Mills, Lorentz, French Creek, Cedarville and
Normantown.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 79 between mile markers 77 and 104. Route 33 between mile
markers 1 and 7.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 10 at 11:55PM CDT until September 11 at 12:30AM CDT by NWS Paducah KY
properties.description:
At 1155 PM CDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from 6
miles north of Parma to over Marston, or along a line from 10 miles
east of Bernie to 6 miles northeast of Portageville, moving northeast
at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Sikeston, Portageville, New Madrid, Lilbourn, Hunter-Dawson State
Historic Site, Parma, Matthews, Marston, Howardville, Risco,
Canalou, Farrenburg, Catron and North Lilbourn.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. These storms are capable of producing damaging winds.
